recreation_prompts.t2i_start_frame: A flat 2D illustrated Korean male character depicted from the chest upward, positioned in the right sixty percent of a wide 16:9 frame against a pure white seamless background. The character has a rounded, slightly boxy face with minimal facial features rendered entirely as bold cobalt-blue outlines on a white face surface — features include two small oval eyes represented by open ellipses, a flat horizontal nose bridge indicated by two short vertical strokes, and a downturned grimace mouth rendered as a thick curved stroke suggesting worry and mild alarm. Dark medium-length hair rendered in solid cobalt-blue sits flat atop the head with a clean silhouette. The ears are simple curved bracket shapes. The character wears a simple collared casual jacket illustrated with a flat fill of cobalt-blue and dense halftone dot shading in a muted periwinkle-blue on the collar, shoulder seam area, and lapels, giving the illusion of shadow without actual shading gradients. The character's right arm is raised toward mid-chest height, and the hand grips a rectangular smartphone outline with the screen facing the viewer — the phone body is drawn with bold cobalt-blue outlines and no screen content visible in this exact frame. The overall posture conveys a person reading a message with a combination of suspicion and unease — shoulders slightly raised and hunched inward, head tilted fractionally downward toward the phone. On the left side of the frame in the generous white negative space, a rounded-corner speech bubble with a bold cobalt-blue border contains three lines of Korean text in a clean rounded sans-serif typeface at approximately 18-20pt size in the same cobalt-blue color. The text reads verbatim: '장미칼 3종세트 주문하셨죠? OO은행 1011-0101-1111011 으로 39,900원 입금해주세요.' followed by a smaller timestamp '오후 4:32' positioned at the lower right of the bubble interior. The speech bubble tail points to the right, toward the character. The composition places the figure on the right half with the figure cropped just above the waist, and uses approximately forty percent of the frame as pure white negative space on the left for the text element. No drop shadow, no gradient, no decorative border on the overall frame. The halftone dot pattern appears on the character's jacket torso, collar, and the back of the hand — rendered as small evenly-spaced circular dots of a lighter blue-grey (#D0D9E8 range) over the cobalt-blue base. The color grade is strict monochrome: all elements — character, outline, speech bubble, typography, halftone dots — exist only in varying values of a single cobalt-blue hue family on pure white. No warm tones, no other accent colors, no red, no green. Illustration style: Korean commercial television animation, flat graphic design sensibility, bold consistent line weight approximately 3-4pt at full resolution, halftone texture evocative of offset print or comic book printing, Korean webtoon and graphic novel visual influence. The atmosphere is anxious and slightly comedic in tone — the visual language of concern and the absurdity of a suspicious payment request coexist. No photographic elements, no real human faces, no identifiable brand logos or trademarks visible on any device or clothing.

inferred_creative_thinking.insight: People trust what they understand; a confusing bank transfer process is fertile ground for fraud — make the process so simple that scams become self-evident
inferred_creative_thinking.persona: Urban Korean smartphone user who has experienced or fears receiving phishing payment requests, values speed and clarity in financial apps
inferred_creative_thinking.moment: Receiving a suspicious-looking payment request SMS and wondering if it is legitimate
inferred_creative_thinking.product_role: Toss auto-recognizes account number and amount from copied text, removing the mental load and reducing fraud risk
inferred_creative_thinking.punchline: The very gesture of 'copy' that scammers exploit becomes the gesture that exposes them — the app shows the mismatch between the stated sender and the actual account owner
inferred_creative_thinking.differentiator: One-tap text copy → auto-fill + name verification: turns a friction point into a fraud-detection moment
inferred_creative_thinking.brand_fit_one_liner: Toss makes sending money as easy as copying a message, and smart enough to protect you while doing it

inferred_brief: Dramatize the new copy-to-transfer auto-recognition feature of the Toss app by showing a realistic phishing SMS scenario that is instantly resolved by the feature, closing with the tagline '송금, 또 한 번 쉬워졌다' to reinforce Toss's brand promise of simplifying finance.
analyst_notes: The ad is a textbook feature-demo narrative compressed into 15 seconds. The phishing SMS hook immediately creates tension and relatability. The 'copy' interaction as the solution pivot is elegant — it turns a universally-understood gesture into a product demo. The monochrome illustration style maintains visual simplicity throughout, preventing cognitive overload. Character callback in the outro (man's face at cut 3 edge) creates visual coherence. Tagline '송금, 또 한 번 쉬워졌다' implies a series of improvements ('once again'), reinforcing brand evolution narrative. Whisper transcription corrected against on-screen captions; specific phishing account number and recipient names preserved verbatim as they are fictitious placeholder data central to the ad's narrative.
